title: 2023 The Last Summer
about: A reflective farewell to my final summer as a State Arts-In Assistant Director, a last chapter I didn't realize was ending while I was living it.
description: After a year away, I returned to State Arts-In and slipped back into a world that still felt familiar: the badge, the work, the early mornings, the late-night office lights, and the friendships that made the exhausting hours worthwhile. At the time, I didn't know it would become my final summer as an Assistant Director. There was no dramatic goodbye or moment when the chapter announced that it was ending. It was simply another year of giving everything I could alongside people I cared about. Eventually life moved in a different direction, not because I loved SAI any less, but because it was time for something new. While the theme that year was Game Show, it was also State Arts-In's 50th anniversary. Rather than giving the track a game-show sound, I chose a more celebratory style to honor the milestone and everything SAI had become over those fifty years. This song looks back on that final summer with gratitude for the work, the laughter, the friendships, and the small moments that became some of the memories I carried longest.
lyrics: One more drive down familiar roads,
One more badge around my neck.
A year away had come and gone,
Still felt like I never left.
The faces changed, the work remained,
You don't count the hours passing
When you're doing it with friends.
Though I didn't know it then.
One more week of giving everything,
One more year with all my friends.
The office lights stayed burning late,
Tomorrow's plans spread on the floor.
The clock kept moving toward the dawn,
Still we found a little more.
We laughed until the room grew bright.
Become the ones you keep for life.
Even those no one else knew.
Though I didn't know it then.
One more chance to build something
Beside a trusted group of friends.
They're simply finding a new way.
In the reason that I came.
Than your heart can answer the same.
The memories were worth every hour,
Some things pay you back in moments,
Even when the work is done.
A chapter closing soft and slow.
Not because I loved it less,
Just because it was time to go.
The fair rolled on without me...
